evidence.discovery_title: John Ternus wants to reshape Apple, here's how - 9to5Mac
evidence.raw_lead: New CEO John Ternus has plans to “overhaul” Apple in an attempt to make it “run faster and leaner,” according...
evidence.title: John Ternus wants to reshape Apple, here's how - 9to5Mac

units.text: New CEO John Ternus has plans to “overhaul” Apple in an attempt to make it “run faster and leaner,” according to a new report from Bloomberg. This includes introducing more products, eliminating “middle-management positions,” and much more.
John Ternus wants to reshape Apple, here’s how

First, the new Apple CEO wants to release more products faster than before, including becoming “more experimental.” One idea is to shake up Apple’s release calendar and rely less on the typical spring-and-fall cadence, instead releasing more new products throughout the year.

Ternus also wants to “create a leaner organization with a greater focus on engineering.” This includes several cost-cutting measures and restructuring. For instance, one change is “eliminating some middle-management positions to reduce the layers separating engineers from senior executives.”

The report says Apple has dismissed “a number of engineering program managers, or EPMs,” in its hardware engineering division over the last two weeks. Bloomberg describes these roles as having been “central to Apple’s product-development process for decades,” responsible for “managing timelines and coordinating work across teams.”

“The cuts affected several program managers, including roughly half a dozen directors, one of the company’s most senior employee levels,” the report says. “Those employees were given just weeks to find other positions within Apple. Those who don’t secure new roles will be laid off later this year.”
Bloomberg says the cost-cutting measures could go much broader than that, though. Ternus has reportedly advocated for Apple to be “leaner” for years:

Ternus, 51, has advocated for a leaner organization for years. While leading hardware engineering, he told employees during an all-hands meeting that Apple should hire fewer people, ask more of its existing engineers and reduce organizational bloat. During a presentation, he showed a slide charting annual headcount growth and argued that the company should be accomplishing more with fewer employees.
Furthermore, Apple reportedly scrapped a plan over the summer to lay off 5,000 AppleCare employees, believing that AI-powered agents could handle those responsibilities.

At the same time, Ternus wants Apple to increase revenue from Apple’s services division alongside Eddy Cue and CFO Kevan Parekh. “They have discussed launching new services and extracting more revenue from existing products and offerings,” the report says.
Ultimately, one source told Bloomberg that things are “hectic” inside Apple right now:

“Everything is a lot more hands-on than it used to be,” said one person familiar with the situation. “It’s hectic right now.” That person and others said managers in product-development groups are being pushed to deliver more products, more frequently and on shorter timelines.
You can read the full report at Bloomberg. It’s a fascinating piece that I highly recommend reading in full.

evidence.discovery_title: Apple Pay Now Available in India With Axis Bank Cards
evidence.raw_lead: Apple Pay is now available in India, which means customers with an eligible card can add it to the Wallet app on iPhone and Apple Watch for contactless and online payments. To use Apple Pay in India, users will need an Axis Bank credit card on the Visa or Mastercard network. Earlier today, TechCrunch reported that merchants and payment terminals will need to add Apple Pay support, so the service might not work at every contactless payment location.
evidence.title: Apple Pay Now Available in India With Axis Bank Cards

units.text: Apple Pay Now Available in India With Axis Bank Cards
Apple Pay is now available in India, which means customers with an eligible card can add it to the Wallet app on iPhone and Apple Watch for contactless and online payments.

To use ‌Apple Pay‌ in India, users will need an Axis Bank credit card on the Visa or Mastercard network. Earlier today, TechCrunch reported that merchants and payment terminals will need to add Apple Pay support, so the service might not work at every contactless payment location.
RuPay, India's domestic card network, is not compatible with ‌Apple Pay‌. Major banks such as HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and SBI Card have not added support either.

There have been rumors about ‌Apple Pay‌ expanding to India for about a decade, but regulatory issues made it difficult. India already has a popular digital payment option, the Unified Payments Interface (UPI). UPI is a state-backed payment system that allows funds to be transferred instantly between two bank accounts. UPI handles approximately 84 percent of India's digital transaction volume, and it does not work with ‌Apple Pay‌.

Apple today released new beta firmware for the AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, AirPods 5, and AirPods Max 2. The firmware has a build number of 9B5042a and is rolling out for developers and public beta testers.
There's no word on what's included in the firmware update because Apple doesn't offer notes for AirPods beta releases.

When the AirPods are connected to an iPhone, iPad, or Mac running iOS 26, iPadOS 26, or macOS 26 or later, there is a beta firmware option that can be accessed in the AirPods settings interface. Toggling on beta updates allows users to install the beta firmware.

Firmware updates can then be downloaded by connecting the AirPods to an Apple device and connecting them to power. It can take a few hours for new firmware to be installed because there is no software update option like there is for other Apple devices.

evidence.discovery_title: Craig Federighi on how Apple helps developers make the most of the iPhone Duo
evidence.raw_lead: Apple software chief Craig Federighi said in an interview that he is excited to see what developers will do with...
evidence.title: Craig Federighi on how Apple helps developers make the most of the iPhone Duo

units.text: Apple software chief Craig Federighi said in an interview that he is excited to see what developers will do with the hinge mechanism in the iPhone Duo.
He said an API lets developers read the angle of the hinge with an accuracy of around five degrees, and the ability to read what Apple describes as the “pose” of the device …

Apple itself uses the hinge angle in a number of ways in software, including a feature that became an instant hit: the way the outer screen defocuses into a preview of the inner one as you open the phone. He told Donald Decodes that the feature is subtle but magical.

The goal was not a fancy animation you’d think about, but something you’d perceive automatically: the screen becomes translucent, a window to what’s below. Fundamental to the device is continuity between your experience when it’s closed and what you find when you open it. Seeing through the screen above to what’s about to be revealed below eases that journey in the most natural way. We’re really delighted with how it came out. It’s subtle but magical.
Federighi says he is confident that developers will do creative and exciting things with the hinge information exposed, just as they have with other iPhone data made available to them.

For most developers […] we’re focused on communicating the pose of the device: are you in book pose, on-table pose, tent pose? Developers don’t have to work with how many degrees open it is. By communicating the pose, the frameworks can react automatically and deliver a consistent experience across apps. But for creative experiences, like our own animation, developers can get closer to the raw information […]

We have a long history of exposing gyroscope and accelerometer data to developers, and they’ve made really interesting use of it over time. One of the ways this device expresses itself is through its poses and the hinge, and we’re excited to see what developers do with it.
He said Apple has also worked hard to make it easier for developers to create apps that take full advantage of the iPhone Duo’s capabilities.

We’ve built our platform on high-level frameworks like UIKit and SwiftUI that abstract away many of the harder layout problems, so apps often inherit new behaviors automatically. Over time we’ve added more high-level constructs that adapt automatically, which makes this transition nearly automatic for many developers.
He added that Apple also supports agentic coding tools to enable developers to adapt existing apps almost completely automatically. You can watch the interview below.

units.text: Apple Invites App Updated With Three New Features

The free Apple Invites app for the iPhone was updated today with three new features: shared albums now support full-resolution photo sharing, Image Playground now lets you create photorealistic backgrounds for invites, and guests who need to verify their email can now tap a link in their inbox instead of entering a code.

Released in February 2025, the Apple Invites app makes it easy to invite people to events, such as birthday parties and baby showers. The ability to create an event in the app requires subscribing to an iCloud+ plan with at least 50GB of storage for $0.99 per month, but anyone who receives an event link can RSVP for free on any device.
Apple's full release notes for version 1.12.0 of the app:
• Shared Albums now support full-resolution sharing, so you can relive every moment in stunning detail right in the app. Anyone, including users without an Apple device, can join and contribute.
• Image Playground now lets you create high quality backgrounds in pretty much any style, including photorealistic, so your invite captures exactly the vibe you have in mind.
• Guests who need to verify their email can now tap a link in their inbox instead of entering a code, making it even easier to get into an event.
• This update contains bug fixes and performance improvements.
The update is available now in the App Store.

evidence.title: Apple Invites update leans on iOS 27's new features

units.text: An update for Apple Invites is making it better for users to create invitations and to relive their events in high resolution, with the iPhone app tapping into some of the features of iOS 27.

The introduction of a new operating system version usually is accompanied by updates to Apple's apps to best take advantage of any new features it includes. With iOS 27 now out on iPhones, Apple Invites has undergone the same treatment.
The update to version 1.12.0 released on September 30 includes three main feature changes, alongside the usual bug fixes and performance improvements.

The first is that Shared Albums now support full-resolution sharing, so party participants can share images from the event with each other without the images being made smaller. This applies both to users with Apple devices and those who do not but have been invited to the party.

Image Playgrounds was previously used to generate backgrounds, but that too has been updated. This includes adopting the new photorealistic options, accessible in the normal version of Image Playgrounds too.
Lastly, Apple has made it easier to verify guests' email addresses. While previously they had to enter a code, the verification emails now include a link that can be tapped to do the same thing.
Previous updates include a June change enabling emoji replies and a confetti animation.
Apple Invites is free, weighs in at 113MB, and requires iOS 26.0 or later.

units.text: IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，科技媒体 MacRumors 昨日（9 月 30 日）发布博文，报道称苹果更新邀请（Invites）App，升级到最新 1.12.0 版本，聚焦活动邀请、照片共享与验证流程优化。
IT之家注：Apple Invites 是苹果推出的活动邀请应用，用于创建和管理生日派对、迎婴派对等活动。
本次应用更新升级共享相册功能，现支持全分辨率照片共享。用户可在应用内查看高清细节，任何收到链接的人均可加入并上传照片，包括非 Apple 设备用户。
新版还扩展图乐园（Image Playground）功能，新增照片级逼真背景生成能力。用户可选择几乎任意风格创建高质量背景，让邀请函更贴合活动主题与氛围需求。
Invite 1.12.0 进一步简化邮箱验证流程，宾客无需再输入验证码。需要验证邮箱的用户只需点击收件箱中的链接，即可快速加入活动，降低参与门槛。
本次更新同时包含错误修复与性能改进。应用要求创建活动者订阅 iCloud+ 计划（50GB 起，月费 0.99 美元（现汇率约合 6.7 元人民币）），但接收链接者可在任何设备免费回复参加。

units.text: Apple Music is now available in more countries, with iPhone users in Albania and three others now able to subscribe and listen to tracks.

While Apple does strive to get its services available in as many territories as possible, some are slower to gain services than others. On Wednesday, the list of countries Apple Music is available in grew by four.
Initially spotted by @Aaronp613 on X and confirmed by a check of Apple's Media Services page, Apple Music is now available in Albania, Brunei, Burkina Faso, and Pakistan.
The launches occur a mere 11 years after the initial unveiling of Apple Music in over 100 countries back in June 2015.

The additional countries follow after a number of other changes relating to Apple Music took place in the last few weeks. This includes the testing of countdown clocks for upcoming album drops, as well as the opening of the Apple Music Hall in London.
It's not the only Services-related change on Wednesday, either. Apple Pay has also launched in India, after nine years of negotiations.

units.text: Apple today expanded Apple Music to four additional countries, bringing the service to a total of 172 countries and regions. Here are the details.
Apple Music comes to users in four new countries
As spotted by Aaron Perris on X, Apple today updated its Availability of Apple Media Services support page, adding Apple Music availability to Albania, Brunei, Burkina Faso, and Pakistan.
Apple has launched Apple Music in: Albania Brunei Burkina Faso Pakistan pic.twitter.com/xUpju3JYxh
— Aaron (@aaronp613) September 30, 2026

Perhaps not coincidentally, three out of the four new countries were also in Apple’s list of regions where iCloud+ now includes Apple TV and Apple Arcade at no extra cost, the exception being Brunei, where the Apple TV subscription service remains unavailable.

Today’s expansion also came alongside a significant update to the Apple Music app for Android, with version 7.0 entering beta with the Liquid Glass redesign, a new floating bottom navigation bar and mini-player, and more.

It also came after Apple rolled out Apple Pay support in India, as the company continues to expand the reach of its Services business into new markets, likely an attempt to address a slowdown in Services revenue growth.
To check out Apple’s official list of media services availability across the globe, follow this link.
Apple Music requires an active subscription. You can sign up for $11.99 per month, with 1 month free, or as part of the Apple One bundle.

units.text: The long-rumored Home Hub tablet device seems to contain an assortment of features from across Apple's ecosystem, and a code sleuth has found a connection between it and iPhone Duo.

Apple's Home Hub is expected to be revealed on October 13 as a tablet device that is carried around the home. Rumors suggest it will display content based on who is nearby or interacting with the device, but very little has been shared otherwise.
Code sleuth and leaker pdfu shared that setting up the Home Hub will include creating a Photo Face. The Photo Face is one that will also be used in the new iPhone Duo StandBy feature.
The Photo Face makes sense for the Home Hub, as it will display something when not in use. The code doesn't provide a name beyond a placeholder of "Apple device."

Setting up Apple's upcoming Home device includes a new step: creating a Photo Face. It's the same Photo Face coming to StandBy on iPhone Duo. That might explain why Apple hasn't officially made StandBy available in the simulator. Photo Face requires iCloud Photos. During setup, pic.twitter.com/Zh3cvAcjPx
— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 30, 2026

Users will be able to select from shuffling photos, showing Memory slideshows, or pulling content from shared albums. Then users will get the chance to select photos manually or pick from specific collections or simply use featured photos chosen by the device.

The screenshots are tall and skinny, suggesting a modal shown over content, so there is nothing to derive from the images themselves. However, the previewed images are square, which fits in with previous rumors that Apple's Home Hub tablet could have a square display.
More code leaks

The leaker shared on Monday that code hinted at Apple offering more StandBy faces and configurations, but they were hidden in the device simulator. Based on the latest Photo Face discovery, it seems Apple could be keeping some features hidden until the Home Hub is revealed.
New OS updates mean more code to delve through, and pdfu has shared several discoveries, including how Tap to Pay on iPhone looks on iPhone Duo. It can be done on either display.
iPhone Duo supports Tap to Pay on both displays, featuring an adaptive interface. pic.twitter.com/EmtQWCXe8c
— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 29, 2026
They've also discovered that the Snoopy screen saver on Apple TV will gain audio at some point, though the files aren't available to examine just yet.

These discoveries are likely tied to Apple not always being perfect in its cleanup of pre-release files in beta software. pdfu has been reliable and accurate in finding and sharing discoveries, like finding that Touch ID would be used in the iPhone Duo.

evidence.discovery_lead: Apple's rumored smart home hub will have different faces users can choose from, some of which are similar to StandBy screens planned for the iPhone Duo . Leaker pdfu shared setup screens of the Photo Face said to be for Apple's upcoming home product. Based on the images, users can select from different photo collections, memories, or shared albums for the Photo Face, and those photos will be shown on the device's display. Photos are pulled from iCloud , so iCloud Photos needs to be turned on for it to work. Users will be prompted to set up the Photo Face when activating the device. Pdfu says the Photo Face for the hub is the same as the Photo Face coming to the ‌iPhone Duo‌, and that could explain why Apple hasn't made the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s StandBy mode available in the Xcode simulator yet. This is the first visual of a home hub face we've seen. The hub is expected to have a 6-inch screen, and it will look similar to an iPad except for the square shape and the base. The hub is rumored to have an iMac G4-like half-dome metal base that connects to the display with an arm. Prior rumors have said the home hub won't have a full App Store , but it will support apps and widgets like Calendar, Weather, Music, Messages, Reminders, and more. The device will be able to tell when someone is approaching it, and can distinguish between people in the home to show different widgets for each user. It makes sense for the hub to display a StandBy-like interface when it is not in active use. There will be multiple idle display options to choose from, just like there are now when using the iPhone in StandBy mode. Earlier today , Bloomberg said the home hub interface is "built heavily" around clock displays and photo slideshows, so the Photo Face will likely be an integral part of the device's software. The home hub is rumored to be debuting on October 13 . units.text: IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，消息源 @i冰宇宙 昨日（9 月 30 日）发布微博，爆料称三星 Galaxy S27 Ultra 重量据称增至 218 克，较前代 Galaxy S26 Ultra（214 克）增加 4 克，厚度维持 7.9 毫米。
IT之家基于爆料内容，汇总梳理下三星 Galaxy S2x Ultra 机型的重量和厚度情况：
机型 | 重量（克） | 厚度（毫米）
Galaxy S23 Ultra | 234 | 8.9
Galaxy S24 Ultra | 232–233 | 8.6
Galaxy S25 Ultra | 218 | 8.2
Galaxy S26 Ultra | 214 | 7.9
Galaxy S27 Ultra | 218（爆料） | 7.9（爆料）
消息源还同步分享了 Galaxy S27 Ultra 预估拍摄样张，指出：
可以确认 S27 Ultra 的照片色彩风格就是故意向 iPhone 靠拢，暖色调几乎和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 表现的一样。下面单数是 S26 Ultra，双数是 iPhone 18 Pro Max。你可以将 S27 Ultra 视为苹果这种风格，来感受一下两者的区别。你更喜欢哪个呢？

为了能让你更加明显地体会到 S27 Ultra 拍照风格的大转变，我做了两张图：
